note: synthetic events in `cases` (compactor input), sanitized real digests in `real_digests` (compactor output)

provenance.why: a digest is compactor output, so the events behind a real one cannot be reconstructed: every case below is hand-built or generated, and the real material enters as digests instead (see `real_digests`).
provenance.shapes: hit shapes follow the two supported index layouts (legacy flat db_name / ECS oracle.database.name) as pinned by tests/test_normalize.py

goldens.note: `generated_by` is normalized so a package version bump does not churn goldens; `pattern_versions` is NOT normalized, because a pattern-library change is supposed to be reviewed.
goldens.policy: goldens are the frozen contract: any golden change requires bumping fixture_version here and reviewing the diff in the same change set. rate_anomaly deltas use the current schema only (window_hours / rate_per_hour / baseline_median_per_hour).
goldens.lint: golden/lint/findings.json pins the deterministic provenance-v1 findings for the two deliberately broken pages in tests/fixtures/wiki_lint/

real_digests.what: compactor output captured from the live Oracle fleet (wiki/digests/<db>/<day>.json), replayed by tests/test_real_digests.py through the layers that consume a digest as input: trigger.decide, trigger.digest_needs_escalation, digest_md.render_md, structured.digest_codes and structured.build_prompt. These digests are NOT events, so they cannot drive the compactor — that is what `cases` is for.
real_digests.why: the synthetic cases pin the compactor's own behaviour; these pin the downstream layers against real shapes no hand-built case reproduces — a 1,753-event storm collapsed into one group, 2,714 `noise` listener events, a 23k-character rendered digest that trips the build_prompt truncation, 67 notable groups with an unmatched cap hit, and days that carry no events at all.
real_digests.schema: all seven parse with the current digest schema as written by dbwiki-compactor/0.1.0; `rate_anomaly` deltas already use the window_hours / rate_per_hour / baseline_median_per_hour keys. Key order is preserved from the live files because render_md walks `sources` and `routine_counters` in insertion order.

sanitization.how: deterministic literal/anchored-regex substitution over the raw JSON text, applied once when the file was copied; tests/test_real_digests.py re-checks that no unsanitized token came back.
sanitization.addresses: replacements come from RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 (192.0.2.0/24), which is reserved for documentation and routes nowhere
kept: ORACLE_SID / db names (cdb1, testcdb_s, awrwh) — already throughout the outer repo's tests and docs
ORA-/TNS- codes, messages, templates and group structure — the whole point of the fixture
OFA paths (/u01/app/oracle/..., /u01/oradata/CDB1/...) and the `oracle` software account — Oracle defaults, already in tests/fixtures/cases/ora600_internal_error.json
the `.localdomain` suffix, ES data-stream index names, service names (cdb1.world), client programs (SQLcl, emagent, OMS, perl, sqlplus) and the SOE demo schema
